title.narrative: Gemensamt FN Program Ending Violence phase II
UN Joint Programme Ending Violence phase II

description.narrative: Project outcomes: 1.Women and girls enjoy more effective preventive measures against violence in Albania. 2.All women survivors and those at risk are better protected from all forms of violence and have equitable access to services in Albania. 3.Responsible institutions and actors implement national policies and legislation on VAW in a more comprehensive, inclusive and coordinated way in Albania. 4. The justice system demonstrates increased accountability and effectiveness in addressing all forms of violence against women.

Detta är ett fortsatt samarbete med UN för ett gemensamt program/JP för att stoppa våld mot kvinnor. UN Women är det ledande organet och UNDP och UNFPA deltar. JP EVaW fokuserar på tre av de fyra pelarna i Istanbulkonventionen: 1) Förhindra alla former av våld mot kvinnor; 2) Säkerställa effektivt skydd och tillhandahållande av lämpliga tjänster för överlevande; 3) Stödja utvecklingen och genomförandet av en effektiv och integrerad politik för våld mot kvinnor. Programmet riktar sig till alla kvinnor och flickor som har utsatts för våld. Särskilt fokus läggs på kvinnor och flickor som utsätts för diskriminering på flera grunder och intersektionella former. Dessutom engagerar projektet män och pojkar som centrala förändringsagenter för att främja jämställdhet mellan könen. UN-organen har ett nära samarbete med nationella partner, bland annat ministeriet för hälsa och socialt skydd, justitieministeriet, ungdomsministeriet, utbildningsministeriet, inrikesministeriet, den statliga polisen, lokala myndigheter, nationella människorättsinstitutioner, medier, det civila samhället och gräsrotsorganisationer.

This is a continued cooperation with UN for a Joint Programme/JP on ending violence against women. UN Women is the lead agency and UNDP and UNFPA are participating ones. The JP EVaW focuses on three of the four pillars of the Istanbul Convention: 1) Prevent of all forms of VAW; 2) Ensure effective protection and provision of adequate services for survivors; 3) Support the development and implementation of effective and integrated policies on VAW. The programme targets all women and girls who have experienced violence. It places a particular focus on women and girls who are subjected to multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination. Furthermore, the project engages men and boys as pivotal agents of change in the advancement of gender equality. The UN Agencies collaborate closely with national partners, including the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Youth, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of the Interior, the State Police, Local Government Units, National Human Rights Institutions, the media, civil society and grassroots organisations, amongst others.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
In its third year of implementation, the UN Joint Programme on Ending Violence Against Women in Albania Phase II (UN JP EVAW II) continued to achieve significant results in preventing and addressing violence against women, contributing to the achievement of SDG Target 5.2 and advancing the key pillars of the Istanbul Convention. During 2025, the programme significantly strengthened efforts to prevent violence, protect survivors, and improve policy and legal frameworks addressing violence against women. Key achievements:
- Enhanced service delivery and improved municipal capacities to respond to violence against women (VAW), supported in part by the establishment and operationalization of the second LILIUM Centre in Vlora. Operating 24/7, the centre provides emergency shelter and support services for up to 72 hours.
- National institutions advanced important legal reforms through the adoption of new frameworks addressing all forms of violence against women. Notably, the newly adopted Law on the Prevention and Protection from Violence Against Women and Domestic Violence expands the definition of violence against women and strengthens related legal provisions in line with EU and international standards. The law also introduces innovative elements, including a specific focus on technology-facilitated violence.
- More than 320 perpetrators of violence against women participated in rehabilitation programmes, with behavioural improvements reflected in a 98 per cent non-recidivism rate during the reporting period. In addition, more than 80 men were engaged as community advocates, actively promoting non-violent behaviours and positive social norms, particularly in relation to violence against women.
- Through the programme's support, updated and internationally comparable data on femicide in Albania became available, indicating a decline in the number of femicides in 2024 compared with previous years.
- More than 780 women received direct support services, including legal assistance, psychological counselling, and reintegration support. At the same time, 526 professionals strengthened their capacity to address violence against women at the local level, enabling institutions to apply more survivor-centred approaches to case management.
- The programme reached more than 900,000 people through social media content and online engagement related to ending violence against women. In addition, over 760 individuals participated in in-person awareness-raising activities and publicly took a stand against violence.
- New evidence on the effectiveness of court decisions in cases involving violence against women has also become available. Findings from a two-year court monitoring process revealed significant gaps in the judiciary's capacity to consistently apply legal standards for adjudicating cases related to violence against women.
